## The server

[`server`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/mcp.html#server)
builds an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that gives an outside
client access to Ramabana’s tools. Pass a host to serve its tools. Pass
an agent as well to mount the agent’s own tools. These are the same
objects a turn uses. A client’s calls appear in the same activity feed
and `changes()` report as a turn’s.

[`Agent._record`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent._record)
wraps each tool with `functools.wraps`. The wrapper keeps the tool’s
signature and docstring, and FastMCP builds each tool’s schema from
them. A tool is described in one place. A client sees the same
description as a model. Without an agent, the server builds the tools
from the host with
[`tools_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/tools.html#tools_for).

`readonly` defaults to True. The client is another agent, and this
server cannot show an approval prompt to the client’s user. Read-only
mode leaves out every write tool. It keeps the read tools and the acting
tools such as `inspect_python` and `generate_image`. With
`readonly=False` the server also mounts the write tools, and the
client’s own approval settings stand in front of them. `delegate=False`
leaves out `ask` even when an agent is given. Any other keyword goes to
`FastMCP`.

`INSTRUCTIONS` is the text the server sends to a client when it
connects. It tells the client’s model how to read and edit with these
tools.

### server

``` python
def server(
    host:NoneType=None, agent:NoneType=None, name:str='ramabana', readonly:bool=True, delegate:bool=True, **kw
):
```

*An MCP server over one host’s tools, and optionally over Ramabana’s own
agent.*

The server below runs over
[`FullHost`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#fullhost),
a test host from [testing](04_testing.ipynb). It declares the code,
file, git, memory, notebook, session, shell and web tool groups. The
server is read-only by default. `replace_text` and `create_file` are
absent. Without an agent, the server also mounts shalya’s `legacy` group
(`list_files`, `list_vars` and others) for one release. Clients written
against version 0.1 keep working. `edit_file` belongs to the opt-in
`exhash` group and is not mounted.

``` python
host = FullHost(files={'pkg/sizes.py': 'RESERVE = 16_384\n\ndef threshold(ctx):\n    return ctx - RESERVE\n'})
mcp = server(host)
tools = await mcp.list_tools()
[t.name for t in tools]
```

``` python
test_eq(set(t.name for t in tools) & WRITE_TOOLS, set())
assert {'view_file', 'list_files'} <= {t.name for t in tools}
len(tools)
```

FastMCP derives each tool’s schema from the tool function. The
description is the docstring a model reads in a turn. The parameters
come from the type annotations.

``` python
t = next(t for t in tools if t.name == 'view_file')
t.description.splitlines()[0], t.inputSchema['properties'], t.annotations.readOnlyHint
```

MCP tool annotations tell a client which calls only read, which are
destructive, and which reach the open world. Open-world tools are the
tools in the `web` and `api` groups.
[`_annotate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/mcp.html#_annotate)
sets the annotations from the same catalog entry that approvals and the
activity feed use. A client can use them to decide which calls to ask
its user about. The server below is built with `readonly=False`.
`replace_text` is mounted, and its annotations can be compared with
those of the read tool `view_file`.

``` python
mcp_w = server(host, readonly=False)
{t.name: (t.annotations.readOnlyHint, t.annotations.destructiveHint, t.annotations.openWorldHint)
 for t in await mcp_w.list_tools() if t.name in ('view_file', 'replace_text', 'web_search')}
```

A client call runs through the same code path as a turn. The client
receives the same text the model would receive. `view_file` returns one
`lineno|hash|content` line for each line of the file.

``` python
out = await mcp.call_tool('view_file', {'path': 'pkg/sizes.py'})
print(out[0][0].text if isinstance(out, tuple) else out)
```

A read-only server does not mount write tools. Calling a write tool by
name returns an error. The last line lists the write tools that
`readonly=False` mounts.

``` python
with expect_fail(): await mcp.call_tool('replace_text', {'path': 'pkg/sizes.py', 'edits': []})
with expect_fail(): await mcp.call_tool('edit_file', {'path': 'pkg/sizes.py', 'commands': []})
[t.name for t in await mcp_w.list_tools() if t.name in WRITE_TOOLS]
```

## Skills as resources

The server offers skills as resources. A resource is text a client can
read. A tool is a call that can have an effect. The server publishes
three resources:

- `ramabana://skills` is an index of every skill, with a one-line
  description of when it applies.
- `skill://{name}` is one skill in full. It is the same text
  `read_skill` returns in a turn.
- `ramabana://status` is a JSON summary of the open folders, the mounted
  tools and the skills. With an agent, it also holds the agent’s status.

A client reads the index and fetches only the skill it needs. A model
does the same with `read_skill` in a turn. Without an agent, the server
finds skills in the served folders and in `~/.agents/skills`.

``` python
[str(r.uriTemplate) for r in await mcp.list_resource_templates()] + [str(r.uri) for r in await mcp.list_resources()]
```

``` python
print((await mcp.read_resource('ramabana://status'))[0].content[:200])
```

## The agent as one tool

With an agent passed in, the server also offers `ask`. `ask` runs a
whole Ramabana turn behind one call. The client sends one task and
receives one answer. The tool loop, the tool results and any compaction
of the history happen inside the server. The client never sees them. The
example below uses
[`fake_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#fake_agent)
from [testing](04_testing.ipynb), an agent with a scripted reply. It
needs no model.

``` python
agent, be = fake_agent(replies=['`threshold` is defined in pkg/sizes.py, and subtracts the reserve.'])
full = server(agent.host, agent)
[t.name for t in await full.list_tools() if t.name == 'ask']
```

``` python
out = await full.call_tool('ask', {'task': 'where is the threshold defined?'})
out[0][0].text if isinstance(out, tuple) else out
```

`ask` runs the turn on a worker thread. A turn blocks, and an MCP server
is asynchronous. The client’s one call sent one message to the agent’s
backend.

``` python
test_eq(len(be.sent), 1)
(await full.read_resource('ramabana://status'))[0].content[:60]
```

## Running it

`ramabana-mcp` is the command-line entry point,
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main). It
splits `--root` into folders and serves them over `--transport`, which
is `stdio` by default. `--model` builds a full agent on that model and
turns on the `ask` tool. Without `--model` there is no agent to receive
a task, and the server offers tools only. `--write` mounts the write
tools. The other options build the host the same way the terminal does.

The agent behind `ask` is built with `approve='none'`. This setting
means no approval gate. A turn that `ask` runs can use the agent’s write
tools without asking anyone. `--write` controls only which tools the
client can call directly.

### main

``` python
def main(
    root:str='.', # comma-separated folders to serve
    model:str=None, # model for `ask`; omit to serve tools only
    write:bool=False, # mount the write tools too
    web:bool=True, # let web tools reach the network via fossick
    read_outside:bool=False, # reads may name any path; writes stay inside
    vault:bool=False, # keep reads in a vishalakshi vault
    pii:str='off', # off | redact | refuse PII from the vault, and from shell, Python and web reads a hosted model gets
    pii_ner:bool=False, # --pii also gates titled names, not only patterns
    transport:str='stdio', # stdio | sse | streamable-http
    cfg:str=None, # config dir, for skills and extensions
):
```

*Serve Ramabana tools over MCP.*

A client that launches its own servers needs the command and its
arguments. This configuration serves one repository and runs `ask` on a
local model:

``` json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ramabana": {
      "command": "ramabana-mcp",
      "args": ["--root", "/path/to/repo", "--model", "qwen-4b"]
    }
  }
}
```

The defaults are read-only tools and no model:

``` bash
ramabana-mcp --root .
```
